The basics of cooling checks at the skyport
The desk wrote this for busy families
Companion Animal Travel Desk: Cooling checks for companion travel

Keeping a pet comfortable at the skyport starts with simple preparation. Aurelia Skyways asks travelers to arrive with water, a secure carrier, and a clear plan for the handoff. The Companion Animal Travel Desk can help you understand what the staff will look for and what you can do before you reach the counter.

Before travel, check the carrier for clean bedding, sturdy latches, and enough airflow. If your pet is sensitive to heat, avoid long waits in warm areas and keep the carrier out of direct sun while you move through the terminal. A calm pet is easier to monitor, so speak softly and keep the routine familiar.

At check-in, staff may review the animal's condition and note any service changes in the desk ledger. <<FACT F012>> Bring any required papers in an easy-to-reach folder so the process stays smooth. If the pet has a care routine, share it clearly with the agent and keep the instructions brief.

Cooling support matters most when the pet is resting or moving between locations. Use absorbent liners if needed, offer water when allowed, and watch for signs of stress such as heavy panting or trembling. If your pet seems unwell, tell the nearest staff member right away so the team can respond in a careful way.

Some travelers worry about holding space and quarantine handling, but the desk keeps these steps organized for safe service. <<FACT F030>> Staff will guide you on where to go next, and they will explain any movement restrictions in plain language. If you are traveling with a young child and a pet, ask for help before the line grows long.

Aurelia Skyways aims for dependable companion travel, and the Companion Animal Travel Desk is ready to support that goal. For more help, contact the Companion Animal Travel Desk before departure or ask the skyport service counter for direct assistance.
